events.text: bonding vs crown for a chipped tooth, when do they do which?

Bonding is for small chips; a crown is for big damage or a weakened tooth.
- Bonding: tooth-coloured resin is shaped onto the tooth and hardened with a light. One visit, little or no drilling, lasts roughly 5 to 10 years.
- Crown: a cap over the whole tooth, used when a large part is missing, there's a crack into the pulp, or after a root canal. Usually two visits.
- For a baby tooth that will fall out in a few years, dentists often just smooth the edge or bond it, and only do more if the nerve is exposed or it hurts.
- Leo's front teeth at 7 may already be adult incisors, which makes the dentist more careful about protecting it.

can't sleep. how does an interac e-transfer move money between two banks? instant for real or IOUs?

It's instant for the person receiving it, but the banks settle with each other later in batches.
- When you send, your bank debits you right away and Interac's network tells the recipient's bank the transfer is good.
- The recipient's bank credits them immediately, trusting the network's guarantee. So yes, it's effectively an IOU between the two banks for a few hours.
- The banks then net out all those obligations and settle through Payments Canada's systems (historically ACSS, now moving to Lynx and the Real-Time Rail) in scheduled cycles during the day.
- That's why there are per-transfer limits: the network is carrying credit risk until settlement.
Short version: real money for you, deferred settlement for the banks.

events.text:
tl;dr in 3 bullets?

The Quiet Cost of Status Meetings

Most product teams don't decide to have too many meetings. They accumulate them.
A standup gets added during a crunch. A weekly sync is created for a launch and never removed.
A 'quick alignment' call becomes recurring because nobody wants to be the person to cancel it.

We surveyed 212 product managers across 40 companies about their calendars.
The median PM spent 14.5 hours a week in recurring meetings.
Of those hours, respondents said 38% were 'mostly status', meaning information that could have been written.
Only 21% of recurring meetings had been reviewed in the past six months.

The cost isn't only the hours. It's the fragmentation.
A PM with four 30-minute meetings spread across a morning has no block longer than 50 minutes.
Deep work, like writing a spec or analysing a funnel, needs 90 minutes or more to get going.
Teams with 'meeting-free mornings' reported spec turnaround 1.6x faster.

What worked for the teams we interviewed:
1. A quarterly meeting audit. Every recurring meeting must justify itself or be deleted.
2. Written status by default. Status goes in a doc or channel; meetings are for decisions.
3. Default lengths of 25 or 50 minutes, not 30 or 60.
4. A named owner for every recurring meeting, who must cancel it when it has no agenda.
5. Protecting one long block per day for each PM.

The pushback is predictable.
Managers worry that written updates get skimmed.
Engineers worry that decisions will happen in docs they never see.
Both concerns are real, and both are solved by the same thing: a clear place where decisions are recorded.

One head of product told us: 'We didn't cut meetings. We cut the meetings that were pretending to be documents.'

The teams that stuck with it saw a second-order effect.
When status moved to writing, the remaining meetings got better.
People came prepared, because there was finally time to prepare.

If you run a team, try one experiment this month: find your oldest recurring meeting and ask whether it still needs to exist.
If nobody can say what it decided last time, you have your answer.

Most recurring meetings are status that could be written, and they fragment the time PMs need for deep work.
- A survey of 212 PMs found a median 14.5 h/week in recurring meetings, 38% of it 'mostly status', and few meetings ever reviewed.
- Fragmentation is the real cost: deep work needs 90+ minute blocks; teams with meeting-free mornings turned specs around 1.6x faster.
- Fixes: quarterly meeting audits, written status by default, 25/50-minute defaults, an owner per meeting, and one protected block a day.

events.text: Priya's old landlord won't return her last month's rent deposit over 'scuff marks'. can he do that in ontario?

In Ontario, no: a last month's rent deposit can only be applied to the last month's rent, not to damage.
- Under the Residential Tenancies Act, landlords can collect a rent deposit (max one month) but not a damage deposit.
- If Priya paid her last month with that deposit, there's nothing to return. If she paid the last month separately, the landlord owes it back, plus any unpaid interest.
- Scuff marks are normal wear and tear; for real damage he'd have to apply to the Landlord and Tenant Board.
- Her move: a written demand letter, then an LTB application (form T1) if he doesn't pay.
I'm pulling the LTB's own guidance page in the background so she has something official to cite.

events.task: Find Ontario LTB guidance on rent deposits
events.report:
Source: Landlord and Tenant Board brochure 'Rent Deposits' (tribunalsontario.example.ca).
A landlord can only use a rent deposit for the rent for the last rental period.
Landlords must pay interest on the deposit yearly at the rent increase guideline rate.
A landlord cannot keep a rent deposit for damages.
Tenant remedy: form T1, 'Tenant Application for a Rebate of Money Owed', within one year of moving out.
Filing fee: $53 online.

why do clocks change on different weekends in Canada and Europe? confuses me calling Lisbon

Because the rules are set separately: North America changes on the first Sunday in November, the EU on the last Sunday in October.
- Canada (following the US since 2007): clocks go back on the first Sunday of November, forward on the second Sunday of March.
- EU and Portugal: back on the last Sunday of October, forward on the last Sunday of March, all at 01:00 UTC at once.
- So for about a week each autumn, and two to three weeks each spring, the usual gap shrinks by an hour.
- Toronto to Lisbon is normally 5 hours; this year from 25 Oct to 1 Nov it's 4 hours.
